title: The innate immune response

draft.title: The innate immune response
card: The innate response starts within minutes of a pathogen getting past the first line of defence. It treats every invader in the same way, so it is non-specific.
damaged or infected tissue releases chemicals that widen blood vessels and make them leakier. More blood flows in, so the area turns red, warm and swollen, and white blood cells can reach the site.
white blood cells that engulf pathogens and break them down inside the cell. They are drawn to the site of infection.
a raised body temperature during infection. It can slow the growth of some pathogens and may help immune cells work.
draft.remember: The innate response is fast and the same for every pathogen: inflammation, fever and phagocytes.

a.q: Why is the innate immune response described as non-specific?
opts: It responds in the same way to any pathogen
It only responds to pathogens met before
It makes a different response for each pathogen
It only acts on pathogens inside body cells
a.why: The innate response does not need to recognise a particular pathogen, so it acts the same way against any invader. Responding differently to each pathogen describes a targeted response, which is not what the innate response does.
a.clue: Think about whether the response changes with the type of invader.

b.q: Sam scrapes his knee on gravel. Within an hour the area is red, warm and swollen. What is the main reason more white blood cells can reach the wound?
opts: Blood vessels widen and become leakier
The body temperature rises across the whole body
Antibodies are made against the gravel
Skin cells engulf the bacteria in the wound
b.why: Inflammation widens blood vessels and makes them leakier, so more blood and white blood cells reach the injured tissue. Fever is a raised body temperature, but it is a different part of the response and does not explain the local redness and swelling.
b.clue: Look at what happens to blood vessels near the wound.

a.best: It responds in the same way to any pathogen

b.best: Blood vessels widen and become leakier
